---
title: 'Colors, Themes, and Decorations'
description: 'Distinguish preset identity, widget decoration, and published theme variants'
---

GitAscii has three separate styling choices:

| Setting                                        | Purpose                                                                                                       |
| :--------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `templateId`                                   | Selects a registered starting layout, such as `native` or `minimal_luxe`.                                     |
| `globalStyles.templateStyle`                   | Selects wrapper decorations recognized by `WidgetRenderer`, such as terminal marks or rounded-card treatment. |
| `renderSvg(..., { theme: 'dark' \| 'light' })` | Selects the rendered variant, including the root background.                                                  |

The editor publishes both `dark.svg` and `light.svg`. README `<picture>` media queries choose the file. Fixed widget colors are not universally recolored by the theme option, so verify contrast in both outputs. `themeMode: 'auto'` and recognized adaptive colors affect the engine's background handling; they do not imply that every third-party card supports automatic theme adaptation.

Use the [current catalog](/templates/overview) for valid template IDs. Older examples using `dracula`, `synthwave`, or `tokyonight` as GitAscii presets do not describe the current registry. An external card may independently accept similarly named upstream themes.

For individual properties, see [configuration](/api/configuration), [rendering](/api/rendering), and [external integrations](/widgets/external-widgets).
